clue.text: Newcastle, Liverpool and Derby on longer the country's leaders

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Duke of Newcastle, Lord Liverpool and the Earl of Derby, three past heads of government
second meaning: those who head the nation's government

explanation.surface: Three northern and midland cities, once great powers, are no longer the nation's leading lights.
explanation.walkthrough: The place names are titles: the Duke of Newcastle, the Earl of Liverpool and the Earl of Derby all headed British governments. 'on longer' is presumably meant as 'no longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of British governments are those who led the nation, and these three noblemen all held that office in the past.

clue.text: Berkshire, perhaps, at the heart of the game

parts.note: the Berkshire is a breed of pig
at the heart of something means in its centre

explanation.surface: An English county sits at the centre of some sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire looks like the county west of London, but it is a pig breed. Pig in the middle is a playground game where one player tries to intercept a ball thrown between two others.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig in the middle is a children's ball-throwing pastime, so it is a game.

clue.text: Club in Gateshead, say, for evening out

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
taken as written
read as gate's head, the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: A nightclub in the town of Gateshead, on Tyneside, is suggested for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town opposite Newcastle, but here it is split into 'gate's head', its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot iron smooths away creases, so it is a flattening or levelling of the fabric.

clue.text: Descriptive of hideout, we hear

parts.note: surface reading: a hiding place or den
setter's reading: spoken, the word splits into hide out, the outer layer of skin

explanation.surface: Someone describes a secret lair as it is rumoured to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a pause, hideout becomes 'hide out': hide is skin, and the outer skin is the epidermis.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the epidermis, the outermost covering layer of skin on an animal's body.

clue.text: Brutal article following popular song without words

indicators.note: following means the article is placed after the other pieces, at the end

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
humming a tune is singing without lyrics
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A savage piece of writing follows a wordless chart hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cruel and pitiless lacks normal human compassion, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Unsound reasoning, when sick, to go up in charge

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An argument that, if you feel ill, you should take charge makes little sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Faulty thinking that fails to follow rational principles lacks sound argument, which is what this noun names.

clue.text: Streetcar soft for the bum?

parts.note: a streetcar is the American name for a tram
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A cushioned tram seat would be kind to one's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum looks like the British word for bottom, but here it is the American word for a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a bum is a homeless wanderer, which is exactly a vagrant beggar.

clue.text: Fried meat cake king is exclusive

parts.note: R for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
sole rights are exclusive rights

explanation.surface: A monarch insists on having a particular dish all to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small patty of minced meat coated in breadcrumbs and fried, a standard dictionary sense.

clue.text: Upside down, some butterflies make marks on paper

parts.note: inverted means turned upside down
the comma is a butterfly species, named for a white mark on its wing

explanation.surface: Butterflies hanging upside down leave traces on a sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks are punctuation written around speech, so they are marks made on a page.

clue.text: Very small, like a Swiss banker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tiny, like a garden dwarf
second meaning: Swiss financiers were nicknamed the gnomes of Zurich

explanation.walkthrough: 'The gnomes of Zurich' was a 1960s British jibe at Swiss bankers thought to be speculating against the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes resembling a dwarfish creature, hence tiny, and also resembling the financiers dubbed gnomes in Zurich.

clue.text: One involved with Alison in illicit affair

indicators.note: involved suggests things tangled up together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is caught up with a woman called Alison in an extramarital romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret sexual relationship, often adulterous, which matches an illicit affair.

clue.text: Rumour of English poet for listeners

indicators.note: what is offered to listeners is heard rather than read, so go by sound

parts.note: Alfred Noyes, English poet who wrote The Highwayman

explanation.surface: Gossip about an English poet is spread to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense noise means talk or report spread about, as in noising something abroad, so it is gossip.

clue.text: Sound director gives Margaret a ring

parts.note: Meg is a short form of Margaret
taken as written
to ring someone is to telephone them

explanation.surface: A film's sound engineer telephones a woman called Margaret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound director' reads as a job in film; it is a device that directs sound outward.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped horn channels and amplifies the voice in one direction, so it literally points or directs sound.

clue.text: Chime gone off, denoting leadership in the league

indicators.note: a chime that has gone off has gone wrong, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bell has sounded, signalling which team tops the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: League here means a league of states, where one dominant member holds sway over the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegemony is dominance of one state within a confederation, so the adjective describes that supremacy among allies.

clue.text: Do church leaders take sustenance?

parts.note: the opening letters of church, also its usual abbreviation
to eat is to take nourishment

explanation.surface: A question about whether bishops and clergy ever stop to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the auxiliary starting a question, but it is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone in British slang is to con or defraud them, which is exactly to swindle them.

clue.text: Accountant has capital advanced — something to put on a horse

definitions.text: something to put on a horse

parts.note: CA is chartered accountant
the capital of France
to move on is to advance

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper invested money and now wants to bet on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something to put on a horse' suggests a bet, but it is a cloth covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth or harness draped over a warhorse or ceremonial mount.

clue.text: Girl revealing male murder victim in book

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
Abel, killed by his brother Cain in the Book of Genesis

explanation.surface: A girl exposes the identity of a man killed in a crime novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is the Bible, where Abel is the first murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a female given name, so it is a girl in the crossword sense of any woman's name.

clue.text: Beg for bit of bread and cheese spread

indicators.note: just a bit of a word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of bread

indicators.note: spread out means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for a morsel of bread and some cheese spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese spread' looks like a foodstuff; spread is the anagram signal acting on cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to implore or entreat urgently, which is what begging someone does.

clue.text: How the stock ran out all at once?

definitions.text: How the stock ran out all at once?

parts.words: How the stock ran out all at once?
parts.note: surface reading: a shop's supplies selling out in one go
setter's reading: stock is livestock, cattle charging off together in panic

explanation.walkthrough: Stock suggests shop goods selling out, but here it is livestock bolting.
explanation.definitionFit: When a herd of cattle flees in a sudden mass panic, the animals have charged off together in one rush.

clue.text: Prepare for attack and remain next to openings of tower

indicators.note: next to places one piece directly beside the other in sequence

parts.note: to stand is to stay or remain
the opening two letters of tower

explanation.surface: A sentry is ordered to stay posted by the entrances of a tower, ready for an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand to is a military order for troops to take up positions in readiness against an expected enemy assault.

clue.text: Lad near damage beside the kidneys?

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy standing close to someone risks harming their kidneys.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys; the Latin roots mean 'next to the kidney'.

clue.text: Cleanse and check germanium

parts.note: to deter is to check or discourage
Ge is the chemical symbol for germanium

explanation.surface: A lab instruction to clean and inspect a sample of a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Deterge is a rare verb meaning to wipe or wash clean, the root of detergent.

clue.text: Collapse of couple on exciting rides

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first piece follows the second in an across answer
exciting means stirring up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Two people fall ill after thrilling fairground rides.
explanation.walkthrough: Collapse is meant as a state of ruin, as of a building left to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: A building in disrepair has decayed and fallen into ruin through neglect, the state of collapse.

clue.text: Knock run off spin bowler

indicators.note: to spin is to whirl round, so the remaining letters are rearranged
taken off means removed, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction to bash the slow bowler's deliveries for runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin bowler' reads as a cricket term; spin is the anagram signal and bowler the word it works on, once the run is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to jostle or nudge them with a bent arm, a push or knock.

clue.text: Proportion of allowance reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A share of someone's allowance has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, which is a proportion between them.

clue.text: Sluggard told stories about Lincoln

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: told untruths
Abraham Lincoln, known as Abe

explanation.surface: A lazy person made up tales about the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-abed is someone who stays in bed late, an idle lazy person.

clue.text: Remedy for Japanese drama — play idly

parts.note: No, or Noh, is classical Japanese theatre
to strum is to play a guitar casually

explanation.surface: A cure is sought for a Japanese play, perhaps by strumming idly.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet cure, a supposed solution for any problem.

clue.text: Hardy characters do, when leotards become loose

indicators.note: things that work loose fall out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tough types at a gym party find their leotards slackening.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy looks like 'tough', but it is Thomas Hardy, whose 1887 novel bears this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a Thomas Hardy novel names its forest-dwelling cast, so they are his characters.
